question: Syndrome of inappropriate antidiuretic hormone secretion is an endocrine disorder that can present with which of the following abnormalities of water homeostasis?

A 74-year-old man with bipolar I disorder, hypertension, and type-2 diabetes mellitus, who is confused and irritable is brought to the clinic by his son. The patient has a 2-day history of severe vomiting and diarrhea. On examination, he has bilateral tremors of the hand. He is diagnosed with lithium toxicity. 
What is the first line of treatment for lithium toxicity?

answers.option: Whole bowel irrigation with polyethylene glycol (PEG)

question:
A 58-year-old man, who is being treated for a chronic cough presents to the clinic with red-orange discoloration of urine for 1 week. He is quite alarmed by the dark color of his urine and is concerned that he may be experiencing adverse effects of medication on his kidneys. The physician counsels and reassures the patient that this is a harmless side effect of a medication he is using. 

Which of the following medications can cause harmless red-orange discoloration of body fluids?

A patient who was previously diagnosed with schizophrenia returns to the clinic with complaints of persistent delusions, hallucinations, and suicidal ideations despite trials of 2 antipsychotics. 
The physician starts the patient on a different antipsychotic medication and counsels him that frequent monitoring of his CBC for absolute neutrophil count is mandated because of the risk of agranulocytosis. 

Which of the following medication was the patient prescribed?

A 32-year-old female, P1+0, who recently gave birth presents to the clinic with the inability to lactate, headaches, dizziness, and tachycardia. 
Laboratory investigations show low serum prolactin levels. 
Low to normal levels of prolactin levels are seen in which of the following conditions?

A 35-year-old female IV drug user presents to the clinic with a fever documented at 100.8°F, associated with chills and malaise. Furthermore, she has asymmetric polyarthritis, swelling in ankles, toes, and wrists associated with pain on extension.  
On examination, she has vesiculopustular rashes on her trunk and the palmar surface of her right hand. 
What is the most likely diagnosis of this patient?

A 24 year-old-male comes to the office due to numbness on the dorsal aspect of the lateral three-and-a-half fingers, and weakness of extension at the wrist and fingers after receiving an intramuscular injection on his shoulder. 

Which of the following nerves is most likely damaged?

A 30-year-old female who is on spironolactone for the treatment of Polycystic Ovarian Syndrome presents with muscle weakness, nausea, vomiting, and diarrhea. On examination, she has decreased deep tendon reflexes. On laboratory investigation her basic metabolic profile showed:

Serum potassium = 7.1 mEq/L,

Serum sodium = 143 mEq/L, and 

Serum chloride = 119 mEq/L.


What is the first step for the treatment of this patient?

answers.option: Reduction of potassium intake and correction of predisposing factor

question:
A 20-year-old male comes to the clinic with complaints of blood in his urine for 1 day and puffiness around the eyes which has gradually increased for 4 days. 2 weeks ago the patient had a sore throat which resolved spontaneously. 
The physician most likely diagnoses him with which of the following medical conditions?

A 20-year-old male comes to the clinic with complaints of blood in his urine for 1 day and puffiness around the eyes which has gradually increased for 4 days. 2 weeks ago the patient had a sore throat which resolved spontaneously. 

What is the treatment of choice?

A 65-year-old male presents to the out-patient department with complaints of progressive muscle weakness in the limbs, frequent cramps, and muscle stiffness along with progressive dysarthria and dysphagia for 4 months. His symptoms started in the right lower limb and then gradually spread to all limbs. 
On examination, there is wasting and fasciculations of bilateral lower limbs, extensor plantar responses, and exaggerated tendon reflexes. 
After further investigation and confirmation of diagnosis, his physician starts his treatment. 

Which of the following was most likely prescribed to the patient?

A 30-year-old female is brought to the clinic by her husband for her complaints of dyspnea, increased salivation, lethargy, and disorientation. On examination, she appears flushed, her pupils are constricted, her heart rate is 55 beats per minute and muscle fasciculations are present. Her complaints started after her medication dose was increased for a condition that causes diplopia, ptosis, and muscle weakness such that she has trouble brushing her hair and climbing stairs, and worsens over the course of the day. Which of the following is most likely the diagnosis for the condition with which she has presented?

A 50-year-old male presents to the clinic with complaints of poor wound healing followed by infection at the site of injury. Upon further inquiry, you find that he has polyuria, polyphagia, and polydipsia. 
Which of the following changes would be seen first on light microscopy of renal tissue from this patient?

A female patient is brought to the clinic after a snake bite with complaints of oozing blood from the wound site, widespread pinpoint and patchy red spots on her skin, and dyspnea. She appears lethargic, has cold skin, and is diaphoretic. She is immediately diagnosed with disseminated intravascular coagulation (DIC) secondary to envenomation by the snake. 

Which of the following is the most appropriate step in the management of this patient?

A 13-year-old girl is brought to the clinic by her father with complaints of profuse vomiting and diarrhea followed by dyspnea, pinpoint pupils, and palpitations. Upon inquiry, you find that she had mistakenly ingested a pesticide prior to the start of these complaints
Which of the following would be the best investigation to confirm exposure to organophosphates?

A 30-year-old female has been experiencing depressed moods, loss of interest in activities, increased appetite, lethargy, and hypersomnia for a year. Her friends encourage her to get assessed for a mood disorder because she constantly experiences feelings of rejection at trivial social cues, which is now affecting their friendship. The patient however is not convinced that she needs an assessment as she experiences improved moods in response to positive events.

Which of the following mood disorders does this patient most likely have?

answers.option: Major depressive disorder with atypical features

question:
A 22-year-old boy presented to the emergency with irregularly intermittent high fever, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, and petechiae. The symptoms started 8 days after going to Kidney Hill with his friends. Physicians are suspecting a disease that is spread by mosquito bites. Blood smear reports state positive Giemsa staining. 
The patient is most likely infected by which of the following?

A 16-year-old boy presented to the emergency with intermittent high fever associated with vomiting and diarrhea. Physicians are suspecting a disease that is spread by mosquito bites. Blood smear reports state positive Giemsa staining, thereby confirming the diagnosis. 

Infection with which of the following species can cause glomerulonephritis in this patient?

A 23 year-old-male who is an IV-drug-user, presents with complaints of malaise, fever, and discomfort in the right upper quadrant which is not associated with food intake. Examination reveals tender hepatomegaly. Ultrasound imaging shows a hypoechoic solitary lesion in the right lobe of the liver. Liver functions tests show slightly elevated ALP, AST, and ALT. 

Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis for this patient?

An 8-year-old boy, who lives on a farm, presents to the clinic with complaints of abdominal pain and distension associated with nausea and vomiting. 
A few weeks ago he also had a dry cough.

CBC shows eosinophilia, MCV=78 fL, Hb=10g/dL.
Stool samples show the presence of visible oval eggs. 
This patient is most likely infected with which of the following species?

A 5-year-old boy is brought to the clinic for complaints of insomnia at night and restlessness. The patient does not have complaints of nightmares, pain, or fever. Systemic inquiry reveals perianal itching which is worse at night. Examination findings are non-significant except for perianal excoriations. 

The physician is suspecting Enterobius vermicularis infection. Which of the following is the best diagnostic test for this infection?

answers.option: Microscopic detection of ova on cellophane tape applied to perianal region

question:
A 50-year-old male with Diabetes Mellitus comes to the clinic for a regular medical checkup. On examination, the patient has a BMI of 29, bilateral and yellow plaques on the eyelids. 


The physician orders a lipid panel to check for blood levels of LDL-C and triglycerides. 
If reports show an increase in LDL-C, which of the following drugs should the patient be started on?

A 34-year-old woman presents to the outpatient department for a check-up 1 year after she had been prescribed fenofibrate for a medical condition that causes deranged lipid profiles. She tells you that she often forgets to take her medication. 

Furthermore, she tells you that her maternal uncles have deranged lipid profiles for which they take medications. 

On physical examination, her height is 5'4" (163 cm), weight is 82 kg (180 pounds) and BMI is 31.6. She has bilateral yellow plaques on her eyelids and nodular, firm, painless swellings on the extensor surfaces of her hands. 

Laboratory studies are significant for triglycerides = 1100 mg/dL (12.43 mmol/L).

Which of the following conditions is this patient most likely at risk of developing?

A 73-year-old patient recovering from an ischemic stroke is brought to the ER by her son for complaints of impaired perception of reality, forgetfulness, and weakness. According to her son, the patient has been insisting she can fly and has been appointed by God to save the town from a dangerous gang. She also insists that he can see cloaked individuals who stalk her with knives to kill her. 

On investigation, her GCS is 14/15 and her vital signs are normal. She has diminished motor function which can be associated with her recent ischemic stroke. 

The physician diagnoses her with psychosis as a complication of the ischemic stroke. 
Which of the following signs are characteristic of psychosis?

answers.option: Delusions present for more than 2 weeks without symptoms of mania and depression

question:
A 27 year-old-female presents to the clinic with complaints of fever, chills, nausea, right lower quadrant abdominal pain, and dark-colored urine. She also complains of dysuria and urinary urgency. 
On examination, her vitals are: Pulse rate = 95/min, blood pressure = 100/80 mmHg, temperature = 100ºF, and respiratory rate = 18/min. The abdominal exam is significant for right costovertebral tenderness. 
Urine D/R shows WBC = 8/hpf, the presence of WBC casts, positive nitrites, and hematuria. The urine β-HCG test is awaited. 

Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis of this patient?

A 55-year-old female patient with asthma and hypertension is being evaluated for her complaints of recurrent attacks of retrosternal chest pain that radiates to her jaw and is triggered by exercise or climbing stairs. The pain is relieved by sitting down or resting. 
The medical student rotating with the physician is asked to list the medications which can be used to manage this patient's symptoms. 
Which of the following medications is the least safe to use for this patient?

A 55-year-old patient is recovering from non-valvular atrial fibrillation. She is currently on warfarin and esmolol. Her most recent INR level = 7. 
What is the next best step in the management of this patient?

A 50-year-old female presents to the clinic with complaints of hemoptysis and hematuria.  Upon further inquiry, the patient tells you that she was diagnosed with allergic rhinitis when she was 26 years old. Which of the following is the best diagnostic test?

answers.option: Serum anti glomerular basement membrane (anti-GBM) antibodies

question:
A 72-year-old patient, with diabetes mellitus and hypertension, presents to the clinic with complaints of symmetric loss of sensation in distal extremities. 
The loss of sensation was initially only in the lower extremities but has now also started in the upper extremities. She sometimes also experiences a burning sensation in her feet, especially at night. 
She is currently taking metformin, lisinopril, and atorvastatin, but she tells you that she frequently forgets to take her medications. 
Her most recent laboratory reports show: fasting blood sugar level = 160 mg/dL and HbA1C= 7.6% 

What is the most likely diagnosis for the complaint the patient has presented with?

A 14-year-old boy presents to the clinic due to excessive bleeding from a wound. He tells you that he often gets bruises, especially on his knees and elbows. This patient most likely has a deficiency of factor VIII. What is the inheritance pattern of this disease?

A 35-year-old female presents to the clinic with complaints of palpitations, heat intolerance, unintentional weight loss, and a painful mass in her neck. The pain is increased by swallowing and coughing and radiated to the jaw. On examination, the mass moves upon swallowing and is tender. Her hands are clammy, her heart rate is 98 beats per minute and her blood pressure is 140/110 mmHg. 
Her serum TSH is low, free T3 and T4 levels are markedly increased, and ESR is increased. A Radioiodine uptake (RAIU) study shows decreased iodine uptake. 

What is the most likely diagnosis of this patient?

A 71-year-old male presents to the clinic with complaints of unintentional weight loss, recurrent infections, lethargy, and night sweats. On examination, he has painless cervical and supraclavicular lymph node enlargements and the liver border can be palpated 1cm below the costal margin. 
Laboratory investigations show WBC = 15000 cells/mm3, lymphocytes = 8000 cells/mm3, Hb = 9 g/dL, blood smear shows a high percentage of small, mature lymphocytes, and the presence of smudge cells. 

What is the most likely diagnosis of this patient?

A 28-year-old female, who is currently pregnant, and in her 1st trimester of pregnancy, came to the clinic for a screening test. She has no active complaints except morning sickness. On urinalysis of mid-stream urine, the presence of E. coli and neutrophils was detected. 

What is the next best step to managing the patient's asymptomatic urinary tract infection?

answers.option: Ultrasound of the kidneys and bladder

question: A 23-year-old male was brought to the emergency department by his parents after he had an episode of generalized rhythmic movements followed by a loss of consciousness. His episode of transient loss of consciousness has self-resolved and the patient is now drowsy and fatigued. He is now being assessed for a seizure disorder. The patient tells you that he initially experienced a short episode of anxiety and seeing bright colorful lights. Soon after he started experiencing lip smacking and involuntary movements of only his right hand which then spread to the whole right upper limb. His parents tell you that soon after, the patient lost consciousness, and the rhythmic muscle jerks spread throughout his body.  However, the patient denies any memory of the generalized muscular jerking. What is the most likely classification for this seizure disorder?

answers.option: Focal to bilateral tonic clonic seizure
Epilepsy with generalised tonic clonic seizures alone

question:
A 29 year-old-patient, who is 15 days post-op after delivering a baby via c-section, presents to the clinic with complaints of localized swelling in her right lower limb. The swelling has increased in size over 2 days and is associated with pain and erythema. On examination, the swelling is warm to the touch and tender, and the circumference of the affected leg is 5 cm larger than the unaffected leg. 
Which of the following is the preferred initial test in this patient for establishing diagnosis?

answers.option: Doppler ultrasound scan of lower limb

question:
A 40-year-old patient presents to the clinic with complaints of headache, decreased libido, and frequent episodes of hypoglycemia. He mentions that he has had to increase hat, ring, and shoe sizes twice now.

A patient presents to the clinic with complaints of fatigue and exertional dyspnea. On examination, she has yellow discoloration of skin and sclera, subconjunctival pallor, and her spleen can be palpated 2cm below the costal margin. 
The physician suspects intravascular hemolytic anemia and prescribes the relevant laboratory workup. 
Which of the following findings does the physician not expect to see on laboratory reports?

A 78-year-old female presents to the family medicine clinic with complaints of ulcers on her foot which are healing poorly and loss of sensation in the distal lower extremities. A monofilament test shows diminished sensation in right lower limb up to her ankles and weak pulses in the dorsalis pedis and posterior tibial arteries of the right lower limb. 

Her most recent laboratory report shows random blood glucose = 218 mg/dL, fasting blood sugar = 188 mg/dL, and HbA1C = 7.8%. 

Which of the following specialist should this patient be referred to for her presenting complaint?

A young female presents to the clinic with complaints of exertional dyspnea, fatigue, and diarrhea. Stool examination shows the presence of proglottids. CBC shows Hb = 8 g/dL, MCV = 110, presence of hyper-segmented neutrophils and eosinophilia. The physician is suspecting a worm infection. 
Which of the following species is this patient most likely infected by?

A 40-year-old male presents with presents to the clinic with complaints of fever, vomiting, and fatigue for 5 days. On examination, there are petechiae and pallor. Laboratory reports show Hb = 9 g/dL, Platelets = 19,000/mm3, Cr = 6 mg/dL. 

What is the most likely cause of this patient's anemia?
Which of the following features will be present in a patient with acute anticholinergic poisoning?

A 16-year-old girl presents to the clinic with complaints of fever and loin pain for the past few days. The abdominal examination reveals tenderness on palpation in the right lower quadrant. What is the most likely diagnosis for this patient?

A patient presents with complaints of fever and loin pain for a few days. The abdominal examination reveals tenderness on palpation in the right lower quadrant. Which of the following investigations would be most appropriate to confirm the diagnosis?

A 45-year-old patient presents with orange-colored sweat and tears. Which of the following drugs is most likely responsible for the orange-colored secretions?

A 25-year-old intravenous (IV) drug user presents to the clinic with fever, migratory polyarthralgia and pustular skin lesions. The physical examination reveals tenosynovitis. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 45-year-old male patient has been prescribed medication for his anxiety and sleep disturbances. However, after discontinuing this medication, he began to experience significant withdrawal symptoms, including agitation, tachycardia, hypertension, and irritability. Which medication is most likely responsible for these symptoms?

A 35-year-old patient presents with complaints of abdominal distension, intermittent abdominal pain, and chronic diarrhea. On general physical examination, pallor can be appreciated. The patient's dietary history reveals a recent intake of undercooked freshwater fish. What worm infestation is most likely responsible for these symptoms?
Which of the following glomerulonephritis is associated with normal serum complement levels?

A 45-year-old patient presents with a history of recurrent infections, easy bruising, and persistent fatigue. Further evaluation reveals anemia. What is the most likely cause of these symptoms in this patient?

A 12-year-old patient presents with a history of fatigue and yellowish discoloration of the sclera. On abdominal examination, splenomegaly is appreciated. An electrophoresis test is performed to evaluate the hemoglobin levels. What is the expected electrophoresis finding in a patient with beta-thalassemia major?

An elderly man is brought to the emergency room with altered levels of consciousness. His initial blood glucose measurement revealed severe hypoglycemia. There is no history of significant weight loss or gain, but he complains of body aches. His insulin levels are high, and his C-peptide levels are low. Family history reveals a 20-year-old son with type-1 diabetes mellitus. What is the most likely cause of hypoglycemia in this elderly patient with altered consciousness?
